newsitem.title: USA: Gateway 2000 down on Lehman downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Gateway 2000 down on Lehman downgrade.

text.p: Shares in Gateway 2000 Inc fell more than seven percent Friday after Lehman Brothers downgraded Gateway to outperform from strong buy, analysts said.

The drop in Gateway's share price occurred a day after the South Dakota-based personal computer distributor announced net income for its third quarter ended September 30 of $0.78 per share, above analysts' consensus estimate of $0.73.
Lehman analyst Kimberly Alexy said she downgraded the stock amid projections for a softer fourth quarter U.S. PC market and new competition in the desktop PC market.
Alexy said she saw Gateway as a "maximum $60 stock given current earnings momentum."

Ashok Kumar, an analyst with Southcoast Capital in Austin, Texas, attributed Gateway's faltering share price to a possible decline in Gateway's profit margins, as indicated by the company's average unit price of approximately $2,500 in the third quarter.

Gateway said Thursday that average unit price declines experienced in the European and Asia/Pacific regions were more severe than in the Americas, resulting in revenue growth significantly less than the growth in unit shipments.

Kumar said the third-quarter average unit price was well below the almost $2,700 realized in the second quarter and was near the average price seen four years ago in 1992, signalling that Gateway's margins were shrinking.
But Kumar was far from bearish on Gateway stock.
"At this price (near $50) you'll see a lot more people engaging the share," Kumar said.
Shares in Gateway were trading down 3-3/4 at 51-3/8.
Gateway declined to comment on the stock activity.
"We don't pay attention to daily swings in the market," said Jim Wharton, director of corporate communications. "We're in the business of making and distributing computers."
